disclaimer: Not financial advice. Research output for entertainment and analysis.
price_provenance_warning: All sportsbook and odds-aggregator sites returned egress-blocked on direct fetch this session. Every price in this file is synthesized from web search result snippets, not read from a book. Treat all numbers as indicative, not executable — confirm at the book before placing anything. Two numbers carried in from the Phase 0 scope check failed verification and were corrected downward (Texas Tech win total 11.5 -> 10.5, Florida State spread -30.5 -> -28.5).
alignment_rule: High confidence requires >=2 threads independently aligned, no thread materially contradicting, and a price with no disagreement flag.

picks.subject: Indiana
picks.reasoning: Defending national champion returns just 56% of production (52nd nationally) per the personnel thread, while replacing Heisman winner and No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza with TCU transfer Josh Hoover, whom sentiment scored public_too_high on generic camp praise. Historical supplies the mechanism: the win-total market pays for storyline over personnel continuity. Three threads align, none contradict, and the price carries no disagreement flag.

picks.subject: Ole Miss
picks.reasoning: Strongest thesis on the sheet, weakest price. Personnel scores Ole Miss +2 net — Pete Golding's internal promotion is the highest-continuity P4 head coaching change of the cycle. Sentiment confirms Trinidad Chambliss cleared for the full season after the Mississippi Supreme Court denied the NCAA's appeal. Historical independently flags a post-Kiffin market bias discounting a CFP semifinalist purely because its star coach left. Downgraded from high solely because two threads disagree on the number by a full win.

picks.subject: Texas Tech
picks.reasoning: QB Brendan Sorsby is suspended for the first two games as a condition of the injunction restoring his eligibility amid an NCAA gambling investigation, verified by sentiment (-2) and personnel (-1) through ESPN and CBS. Honest counterpoint that caps this at medium: those two games are an FCS opponent and Oregon State, backup Will Hammond is healthy, and Tech likely wins both anyway. The edge is the off-field distraction plus an unresolved number on a top-two national win total, not the suspension itself.

picks.subject: LSU
picks.reasoning: Cleanest coach-to-roster fit in the cycle per personnel (+2): Kiffin brought 8 of 11 new staff from Ole Miss including his OC, retained LSU's existing DC, and inherits 70% returning production (7th nationally). Sentiment adds a positive opening camp with transfer QB Sam Leavitt healthy in team periods. Capped at medium because that camp read is a single practice and 8.5 is a harder number in the SEC's first nine-game conference season.

picks.subject: San Jose State at USC (Week 0, 2026-08-29)
picks.reasoning: USC lost projected starting center Kilian O'Connor for the season to a broken leg in camp — verified by sentiment, which scored the market public_too_high on recency. Historical layers the opener dynamic: favorites in lopsided non-conference openers hold back playbook install and protect starters, suppressing large-spread cover rates. A new center calling protections while laying 35.5 is exactly this spot. Capped at medium because the historical support is structural reasoning, not a sourced ATS record.

picks.subject: Julian Sayin (Ohio State, QB)
picks.reasoning: Sayin is Ohio State's first unequivocal returning starting QB since 2022 after a 12-2 freshman season, with uniformly positive insider reporting (sentiment +1). Market prices him behind CJ Carr and Arch Manning at +750 despite his quarterbacking the team with the shortest championship odds on the board (+550/+600). Heisman voting follows team success, so a 2.5-point implied discount to the co-favorites is the value.

picks.subject: Ohio State
picks.reasoning: Sentiment scores Ohio State public_too_low on QB-room certainty and it is the championship favorite, but no other thread corroborates — personnel never sourced Ohio State's returning production. One thread with no support is speculative by rule regardless of how reasonable the thesis reads.

picks.subject: Oklahoma
picks.reasoning: Personnel (75% returning production, 12th nationally) and sentiment (+1, John Mateer healthy and physically transformed) both support the over — but historical directly contradicts, flagging Oklahoma as drawing one of the two most lopsided national Over leans by handle. The market already knows, and -145 is what that knowledge costs. Downgraded from medium on the contradiction.

picks.subject: Penn State
picks.reasoning: Personnel flags a real Year 1 fit tax (net -1): Matt Campbell's run-first Iowa State identity imposed on Franklin's roster with no confirmed staff continuity. But the -134 under juice indicates the market has already priced it, and sentiment is neutral. Sound thesis, poor price — the only win total on the board with verified two-sided pricing, and it says the edge is gone.

picks.subject: LSU
picks.reasoning: Same Kiffin coach-fit thesis as the LSU win-total pick (personnel +2, sentiment +1), expressed as a 20-1 longshot. Speculative rather than medium because a championship future compounds every unmodeled variable across a full season and the supporting camp signal is one practice old.

avoid.subject: Josh Hoover (Indiana) Heisman +1200
avoid.reason: Directly contradicted by the sheet's highest-confidence pick — the Indiana under rests on Hoover being a downgrade from Mendoza.

player_props.reason: Market thread found zero player props posted for Week 0 or Week 1 — expected this far out. None were fabricated. Separately, Illinois prohibits college player props entirely, retail and online, so these markets are unavailable in-state regardless.

parlays.reason: No genuinely correlated multi-leg exists in the sourced data. Indiana Under 10.5 and fading Indiana's +317 Big Ten price are the same thesis twice — parlaying them concentrates one view while multiplying vig. Ole Miss is the one team where a win-total leg and a conference leg would be genuinely correlated, but Ole Miss was not on the sourced SEC futures board so the second leg cannot be priced. An uncorrelated parlay is a worse version of two straight bets.

illinois_compliance.note: Wagers on Illinois-based college teams (Illinois, Northwestern) are in-person/retail only at licensed IL sportsbooks — not available on any online app. Illinois also bans college player props entirely, retail and online.

actionable_trend_without_a_pick.trend: FBS teams playing their season opener against an opponent that has already played a game are 56-33 ATS (62.9%) since 2005. The market overvalues the extra look the already-played team received.
actionable_trend_without_a_pick.why_no_pick: Directly actionable in Week 1 — fade the Week 0 participants (UNC, TCU, NC State, Virginia, USC, San Jose State, Hawai'i, Stanford, Memphis, UNLV) against opponents making their season debut. But the market thread never sourced those specific Week 1 matchups, so no bet can be named. Filling in that one slate converts a 63% trend into concrete picks — the highest-value next step.

data_gaps: New-coach Year 1 ATS base rates do not exist in any sourced form. The historical thread searched seven analytics sites and found nothing usable. In a cycle with ~30 new head coaches this is the single largest hole in the model — every coaching-change judgment here rests on structural reasoning rather than data.
Transfer portal position-group data was sourced for only two teams (Oklahoma State, Texas Tech).
Returning production was sourced for only six teams (Texas, LSU, Oklahoma, Georgia, Indiana, Notre Dame).
Win-total juice was verified for exactly one team (Penn State, FanDuel).

Seven of the ten Illinois-legal books (bet365, BetRivers, Caesars, Circa, Fanatics, Hard Rock Bet, theScore Bet) could not be priced at all — only DraftKings, FanDuel and BetMGM were ever attributable.
Game totals and moneylines are missing for nearly every sourced game line.
The Florida State vs New Mexico State game has an unresolved date (Aug 29 Week 0 vs Sep 5 Week 1) in addition to a 2-point spread disagreement.
